title: ASRock Rack SORANOD8-2L2T Review A New AMD EPYC 8005 Sorano Motherboard
gist: Hardware review of ASRock Rack's SORANOD8-2L2T, a single-socket SP6 server board built for AMD's new Zen 5-based EPYC 8005 'Sorano' CPUs (up to 84 cores, 96 PCIe Gen5 lanes, 225W), which trades memory speed (DDR5-5200 via an unusual 8-slot 2DPC layout, up to 2TB) for capacity and adds SATA-capable MCIO ports for dense storage. The captured text covers only the hardware-overview portion of the review (it ends before the block diagram and any performance testing).

insights.claim: AMD's EPYC 8005 'Sorano' line brings full Zen 5 cores to the mid-tier SP6 socket with up to 84 cores and 96 PCIe Gen5 lanes, replacing the Zen 4c-based EPYC 8004 'Siena' and reaching far higher performance levels.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: Upgrades AMD's mid-range/edge server offering from density-optimized cores to full Zen 5, strengthening its position in cost- and power-constrained single-socket deployments.
insights.quote: it replaces the former’s Zen 4c cores with full-fat Zen 5 cores, allowing Sorano to hit far greater performance levels
insights.locator: A couple of months back AMD

insights.claim: EPYC 8005 Sorano is backward compatible with existing SP6 motherboards after a BIOS update, yet some board vendors including ASRock Rack are still launching Sorano-specific boards.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: Drop-in compatibility lowers upgrade friction for installed SP6 fleets, while new boards signal vendors see enough demand to refresh the ecosystem.
insights.locator: While Sorano is fully backward compatible

insights.claim: SP6 processors top out at 225 watts, so SP6 boards need only basic VRM heatsinks and non-exotic power delivery relative to higher-end server sockets.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: Lower power envelope keeps SP6 platforms cheaper to build and cool, suiting them to edge, storage and cost-sensitive servers.

insights.claim: Although SP6 is natively a 6-channel memory platform, ASRock Rack uses 8 RDIMM slots on all its SP6 boards because a 7-PCIe-slot layout lacks room for 12 DIMMs, enabling up to 2TB of memory in a '2DPC-ish' configuration.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: Board-level design choices, not just CPU specs, determine usable memory capacity on mid-tier servers.
insights.quote: A traditional 7 PCIe slot layout does not afford enough space for 12 DIMMs, but it does for 8.
insights.locator: As for the purpose behind 8 slots

insights.claim: Running as a 2DPC board caps the SORANOD8-2L2T at DDR5-5200, versus up to DDR5-6400 on 1DPC SP6 boards, trading memory bandwidth for capacity.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: Buyers of memory-bandwidth-sensitive workloads should weigh 1DPC alternatives; capacity-bound workloads benefit from the 2TB ceiling.

insights.claim: The SORANOD8-2L2T exposes all 96 of Sorano's PCIe Gen5 lanes: four Gen5 x16 slots plus one Gen5 x8 slot (72 lanes) and two MCIO x8 connectors (the remaining 16), alongside two M.2 Gen5 x4 slots.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: Full lane exposure makes the board a flexible base for GPU, NIC or NVMe-heavy single-socket builds.
insights.locator: First and foremost, ASRock Rack has equipped

insights.claim: New versus its Siena-era predecessor, the SORANOD8-2L2T's two MCIO x8 connectors can be switched to SATA signaling, each becoming an eight-port SATA 6Gbps host for up to 16 additional SATA drives, while the top PCIe slot can also provide 16 SATA ports via a riser card.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: Positions the board for high-density HDD/SATA storage servers, indicating continued demand for cheap bulk SATA capacity alongside NVMe.
insights.quote: allowing for up to (another) 16 SATA drives, ideal for high-density storage servers
insights.locator: For the final set of storage options

insights.claim: The top PCIe x16 slot on the SORANOD8-2L2T supports CXL connectivity in addition to PCIe.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: CXL support on mid-tier boards hints at memory-expansion use cases reaching beyond flagship platforms.
insights.locator: The top slot is a particularly special slot

insights.claim: The SORANOD8-2L2T integrates two 10GbE ports on an Intel X710-AT2 controller and two 1GbE ports on Intel I210 controllers, plus an IPMI port on an ASPEED AST2600 BMC.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: Intel retains onboard NIC design wins on server boards; ASPEED continues as the default BMC supplier.

insights.claim: The ASPEED AST2600 remains the most prevalent BMC seen in server boards passing through ServeTheHome's labs.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: Signals ASPEED's entrenched near-default position in the server BMC market.
insights.quote: The AST2600 continues to this day to be the most prevalent BMC we see in boards that cross our labs.
insights.locator: Farthest to the left is the IPMI

insights.claim: Despite being marketed for both server and workstation use, the SORANOD8-2L2T is clearly server-first: only four 5Gbps USB-A ports, a 4-pin signaling header with a 24-pin ATX adapter instead of a full ATX connector, six 6-pin fan headers, a VGA port, and a 12x10-inch 'ATX-like' size slightly too wide for strict ATX cases.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: Workstation builders will need add-in USB and case compatibility checks; the board targets rack/server integrators.
insights.quote: This is very clearly a server motherboard first and foremost.
insights.locator: For a server installation, this is fine

insights.claim: VGA output still sees significant use in data centers, which is why a brand-new 2026 server board still ships with a DB15 VGA port even though the AST2600 BMC supports DisplayPort.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: Illustrates slow-moving legacy standards in data center operations tooling.
insights.quote: VGA still sees significant use in data centers
